source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text: Following harvest, Pursat orange fruit is sorted, graded by size, and packed before sale. This is scheduled across the full August-September harvest window in the annual calendar, running in parallel with the harvest itself rather than as a separate later step. The program's Good Agricultural Practice (GAP) approach for this stage aims to reduce physical damage to fruit, keep fruit shape/appearance consistent, and avoid chemical residue on the product reaching the point of sale.
